acceptance.condition: The repository contains one Reviewer-specific bounded provider module defining provider invocation/result/error contracts and a one-call attempt function that consumes existing BP6-P3 construct_request/validate_response surfaces without modifying or duplicating P3 semantic authority.

Every valid PRIMARY or DELTA attempt performs exactly one provider invocation and returns only one P3-validated transient AIOS_REVIEW_DECISION plus one bounded immutable attribution; invalid caller/P3 input performs zero invocations and no path can perform a second call.

Transport failure, malformed/oversized native response, P3 semantic-response rejection and provider/model attribution drift each stop after the exact allowed call count with the documented typed reason code, while valid semantic BLOCKED remains a successful Reviewer decision and no error fabricates REVIEW/lifecycle state.

Provider/model identity is immutable per included adapter and checked across the attempt; attribution is closed/bounded and operational-only; changing only provider/model/session/invocation attribution across conforming adapters cannot change P3 request or decision fingerprints.

MappingReviewerProvider and JsonReviewerProvider independently enforce the 262144-byte native response ceiling, closed wrapper extraction, strict mapping/UTF-8 JSON grammar as applicable, 8192-byte attribution ceiling and field bounds, retain no raw native payload and add no provider-specific semantic policy.

Semantic correctness is self-sufficient from the exact P3 request: provider input contains no hidden prior session/history material, operational attribution never becomes semantic input, and equivalent semantic output succeeds on independent fresh adapter instances without conversation continuation.

P4 contains no Brain/Executor authority import, provider registry/router, retry/fallback/failover/voting/second Reviewer call, repository discovery, persistence, verification, ingress, remediation/repair, Runtime or Publisher action on any successful or failing path.

Focused fresh-fixture tests cover PRIMARY PASS/CHANGES_REQUIRED/BLOCKED, DELTA, exact one-call behavior, invalid input zero-call behavior, every typed failure family, configured identity drift, native/attribution bounds, malformed mapping and JSON wrappers including duplicate keys/UTF-8/non-finite values, independent adapter semantic-identity invariance, hidden-session absence, no raw-payload retention, no second-call authority and prohibited-import boundaries.

src/aios_renew/reviewer_provider_protocol.py is the reviewed semantic protocol authority for exact Reviewer request construction/revalidation, provider semantic response validation, transient REVIEW candidate materialization, canonical parse_review round-trip protection and review.validate_review invocation.
Human/configuration selects one Reviewer provider implementation and exact provider/model identity before an attempt begins. P4 does not infer, rank or choose providers/models.
BP-7 owns cross-context/provider hot-swap conformance. BP-8 owns a controlled real non-default provider proof. BP6-P4 proves only non-network contract conformance.

hard: Production mutation is limited to scope.modify. If satisfying this contract requires another production file or any semantic change to BP6-P3/P1/P2, REVIEW, Decision Packet or ingress, fail closed back to Brain.

reviewer_provider.py is transient caller-supplied invocation support only. It performs no repository/Git/GitHub/filesystem/environment/credential/lifecycle discovery, no verification, no persistence and no canonical mutation.

Define a ReviewerProvider protocol exposing immutable configured provider and model identity plus one invoke(request) operation. The attempt function receives one already-selected provider instance. No provider registry, selection or routing function exists.

Define ReviewerProviderInvocation containing exactly two logical values: semantic_response and attribution. semantic_response is the extracted mapping passed unchanged to existing BP6-P3 validate_response. attribution is closed operational metadata only.

Operational attribution contains exactly provider, model, session_id and invocation_id. provider/model are non-empty strict UTF-8 strings <=512 bytes each. session_id/invocation_id are null or non-empty strict UTF-8 strings <=2048 bytes each. The normalized complete attribution mapping is <=8192 UTF-8 bytes.

Provider/model identity is fixed for one configured provider instance. Every invocation attribution must exactly match that configured identity. Identity drift before, during or after the call fails closed as PROVIDER_ATTRIBUTION_MISMATCH and never becomes provider switching/fallback.

Define one ReviewerAttemptResult success surface containing only the exact transient P3 AIOS_REVIEW_DECISION and one immutable bounded attribution mapping. It carries no canonical handoff/publication permission and retains no raw native provider payload.

Define one ReviewerAttemptError with stable bounded reason_code, phase and invocation_count. Required reason codes are PROTOCOL_INPUT_INVALID, PROVIDER_TRANSPORT_FAILURE, PROVIDER_RESPONSE_INVALID and PROVIDER_ATTRIBUTION_MISMATCH. These are pre-REVIEW operational/protocol failures only, never REVIEW/BLOCKED/RUN FAILURE/remediation/publication truth.

attempt(...) receives provider plus the exact P3 constructor inputs: an actual DecisionPacket, review_scope, review_material_package, reviewer_procedure_package, reviewer_return_contract_package, external_bindings and optional prior_review. It uses existing reviewer_provider_protocol.construct_request exactly once before invocation. Any caller/P3 request defect terminates as PROTOCOL_INPUT_INVALID with invocation_count 0.

After successful input construction, attempt captures the configured provider/model identity, verifies it is bounded/valid and verifies provider.invoke is callable. The semantic REVIEW phase then invokes provider.invoke exactly once with a deep-copied exact P3 request. Invocation count increments to 1 before entering provider code and can never exceed 1.

A provider callable/transport exception before a valid ProviderInvocation is PROVIDER_TRANSPORT_FAILURE unless the exact cause is provider/model attribution drift. A malformed/oversized native wrapper, malformed attribution, wrong invocation object, extraction failure or P3 semantic response rejection is PROVIDER_RESPONSE_INVALID unless exact provider/model attribution drift applies.

After the one invocation, attempt rechecks configured provider/model identity, validates the returned closed attribution, then passes only semantic_response to existing reviewer_provider_protocol.validate_response(request, ...). It does not reconstruct REVIEW or duplicate P2B/P3 validation.

A valid semantic BLOCKED response is a successful transient Reviewer decision, not ReviewerAttemptError. Conversely transport/material/response/attribution errors must never be converted to semantic BLOCKED or CHANGES_REQUIRED.

No success or failure path may invoke provider.invoke a second time. There is no freshness supplier, Stage 2, AUDIT_RECONCILE, recursive review, retry, fallback, failover, voting, alternate provider or third call.

Define a MappingReviewerProvider non-network adapter with frozen configured provider/model/callable. It deep-copies the exact request into one injected mapping-native callable, independently validates strict JSON-compatible native values with maximum structural depth 32, enforces the native response ceiling, requires one closed native wrapper exactly {semantic_response, attribution}, validates attribution, extracts a semantic-response mapping and retains no raw native payload.

Define a JsonReviewerProvider non-network adapter with frozen configured provider/model/callable. It canonical-serializes the exact request to strict UTF-8 JSON bytes, invokes one injected bytes callable, accepts only returned str/bytes, enforces the raw native response ceiling before parse, rejects invalid UTF-8, duplicate JSON keys, NaN/Infinity and malformed/non-mapping wrappers, independently requires exactly {semantic_response, attribution}, validates attribution and retains no raw response after extraction.

Both adapters enforce a complete native response ceiling of 262144 bytes before P3 semantic validation. They may share only small identity/size primitives; the mapping-native and UTF-8 JSON native-wrapper extraction paths must not delegate to one common wrapper parser.

The provider receives only the exact P3 request. P4 passes no previous prompt, chat history, native response, reasoning trace, continuation token, session content or provider/model metadata into semantic request material. session_id and invocation_id are output operational attribution only.

Equivalent semantic provider output through the two independent adapters must yield identical P3 request_fingerprint and decision_fingerprint even when provider/model/session/invocation attribution differs. Operational attribution never participates in semantic identity.

Production code must not import brain_provider, brain_provider_protocol, brain_audit, codex_adapter, antigravity_adapter, antigravity_minimax_adapter, execution_profile, authoring_ingress, Runtime operator/dispatch, publication or Git/GitHub transport modules.

Tests must construct fresh mutable Task/packet/package/scope/binding/prior-review fixtures per case. Mutation/adversarial tests must not share mutable semantic fixture state, explicitly avoiding the test-state pollution that caused RUN-183-001 before REPAIR-183-001.

Verification remains Runtime-owned and minimum-sufficient. Executor must not add unrelated/full-suite verification. The required focused suite must prove exact one-call cardinality, stop conditions, typed failures, operational/semantic identity separation, adapter independence and authority boundaries.

task.goal: Implement BP6-P4 as a thin Reviewer-specific provider invocation boundary over the already-reviewed BP6-P3 AIOS_REVIEW_REQUEST / AIOS_REVIEW_DECISION protocol, with exactly one semantic provider invocation per admitted review attempt, bounded operational attribution, fail-closed provider/model identity checks, two independent non-network conformance adapters, and no retry/fallback/router, lifecycle, ingress, remediation or publication authority.
non_goals: Add a real network/API Reviewer integration, SDK client, endpoint, credentials, authentication, production deployment, GitHub carrier/workflow, CLI or downstream adoption.

Add provider/model registry, scoring, ranking, adaptive routing, automatic model selection, retry, fallback, failover, voting, parallel Reviewer calls, provider switch, recursive review, Reviewer-of-Reviewer or any second semantic invocation.
Reuse/import brain_provider, Brain semantic protocol/audit orchestration, Executor adapters or execution-profile routing as Reviewer authority merely to reduce code duplication.

Inspect repository files, Git, GitHub, Unified State, filesystem, environment, credentials, clock/random state or canonical lifecycle from the Reviewer provider shell. All semantic/canonical material remains caller supplied through P3 inputs.
Persist prompts, raw native provider payloads, semantic responses, reasoning, conversation history, sessions, requests, decisions or operational attribution; add a memory/session store.

Modify reviewer_provider_protocol.py, Decision Packet, P1A/P1B/P2A/P2B, canonical REVIEW schema, Runtime, Unified State, Reviewer semantics, authoring ingress, remediation/repair, Publisher, roadmap state or frozen Kernel semantics.

Call SUBMIT_REVIEW, canonicalize the transient REVIEW candidate, author remediation/repair, invoke Runtime verification, publish, or translate provider errors into REVIEW/BLOCKED/RUN FAILURE/lifecycle state.
Claim BP-7 hot-swap conformance, BP-8 real-provider proof or BP-9 downstream adoption.
Push or publish from Executor implementation.
task.problem: BP6-P3 now provides the exact provider-neutral Reviewer semantic request/decision contract and canonical REVIEW reconstruction/validation boundary, but no reviewed layer yet owns the deliberately narrow mechanics of invoking one already-selected Reviewer provider, extracting one bounded provider-native semantic response, separating operational attribution from semantic identity, and stopping after the exact one allowed call. If each future Reviewer integration implements these mechanics independently, adapters could silently gain hidden-session semantics, provider/model routing, retries/fallback, repository discovery, canonical REVIEW identity authorship, or lifecycle mutation. P4 must add only a Reviewer-specific one-call shell and leave real provider deployment, hot-swap and downstream adoption to later milestones.
